claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance during high-temperature exposure in air.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes pesting during high-temperature exposure in air.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Adding 1–3 at.% Si to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance.
Adding 1–3 at.% Si will cause a continuous, adherent silicide layer to form on the alloy surface during exposure to air at 800 °C.
The proposed silicide layer will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The proposed diffusion barrier will reduce oxygen ingress into the alloy.
Reduced oxygen ingress will prevent pesting.
Limiting the Si addition to 1–3 at.% will preserve the alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility.
Limiting the Si addition to 1–3 at.% will preserve the alloy's high-temperature yield strength.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, the Si-modified alloy will have less than 10% of the oxidation mass gain of untreated material.
The Si-modified alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility within 8–16%.
The Si-modified alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed protection applies in air at 800 °C for exposures of up to 5 hours.
The proposed intervention assumes that adding 1–3 at.% Si does not significantly alter the alloy's microstructure or phase stability.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines mass gain below 10% of the untreated value as success, but the falsification rule places 'less than 10%' parenthetically after failure to obtain a significant reduction. The intended failure condition is therefore worded ambiguously and could be read as treating the success threshold as a falsifying result.
